# Reading Átlas the way it was meant to be written
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *atlas*. This is the file on how **Átlas** replaced it.

Átlas belongs to the older generation of gods. His myths are few because he is fixed in place, but his presence shapes the geography and cosmology of the Greek world. Átlas was one of the leading Titans in the war against Zeús and the Olympians.  When the Titans were defeated, Zeús singled him out for the heaviest punishment: he must hold up the sky for all time.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Átlas
- **ASCII form:** atlas
- **Meaning:** "Enduring, suffering (from τλάω)"
- **Domain of influence:** Bearer of the Heavens
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Ἄτλας
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 45 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Ἄτλας**. On the evidence, it means "Enduring, suffering (from τλάω)".

Strip **Átlas** to *atlas* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → Á** — Acute on alpha: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

These are the small, provable things a restoration is made of: not taste, not branding — attestation.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Átlas** lives at [/sites/atlas/](/sites/atlas/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/atlas/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/atlas/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/atlas/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Átlas** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Mapping & Geospatial** — Mercator put Atlas holding the globe on his map book; the industry took the name.
- **Aviation & Aerospace** — The Atlas launch vehicles flew for six decades; the sky-bearer's namesake rocket.
- **Sports, Fitness & Competition** — The Atlas stones are strongman's signature lift; the cosmic burden made sport.

If a match here reads wrong, the atlas says how to challenge it. The patterns are falsifiable — that is what makes them worth publishing.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
